Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality notice from January 2016 for the Georgia-Pacific Muskogee mill at Chandler Road, describing power boilers that co-generate electricity through steam turbines.
Map link to the plant point from the federal file; it falls on the mill site in Muskogee.

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list a plant by this name. The monthly federal generator file for September 2026 lists Georgia-Pacific Muskogee, plant 10362, with three natural gas steam turbines: GEN1 at 25 MW from 1979, GEN2 at 44.5 MW from 1980 and GEN3 at 44.5 MW from 1982. All three are operating. That is 114 MW in total. The plant is at the Georgia-Pacific Muskogee mill, 4901 Chandler Road, Muskogee. A 2016 notice from the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality describes the mill's power boilers, which make steam for turbines that generate electricity. No document shows the units retired. GEM already lists a Fort James Muskogee Mill power plant with two coal units of 45.5 MW that are marked retired in 2020, and its note says conversion to gas. These may be the same turbines. A separate question card asks about that link. The owner is Georgia-Pacific LLC, which already exists as an entity. The status is operating because the federal file says so. The point comes from the federal file, so the location is approximate.
